terms.gloss: be first, hold the first place
terms.grammar: verb phrase: prīmās (partēs), the first part, with tenēre, agere or ferre
evidence: Cic. Brut. 308: prīmās in causīs agēbat Hortēnsius (Lewis & Short s.v. prīmus)
terms.comment: For “be at the head of the class”, where Traupman has classem dūcere, which is classically “to command a fleet”.

terms.gloss: be at the head of the class
terms.comment: In classical Latin classis with dūcere is a fleet led to sea; say prīmās tenēre.

terms.gloss: grade (a year of school, as first grade)
terms.comment: Traupman gives gradus and classis for a school grade.

sources: Lewis & Short: classis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): p. 28; p. 291.
